key: The seven milk a single cow; the two set other five to work, On the stream’s loud-resounding bank.
s: Midway through a hymn to Agni, after his horses and car are seen, the verse speaks in numbers; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.61.7, reads the seven as priests milking the one gharma, and the two, pratiprasthātṛ and adhvaryu, as directing five others, the sacrificer among them.

evidence.gloss: The seven officiating priests milk the one gharma. Among them the two, the pratiprasthātṛ and the adhvaryu, set five others to work, employ them. Who are those five? The sacrificer (yajamāna), the brahman, the hotṛ, the āgnīdhra and the prastotṛ.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Rig Veda 8.61.7 at [680,7]); Sāyaṇa on standard 8.72.7 says the seven ṛtvijs milk the one gharma and the two (pratiprasthātṛ and adhvaryu, as Wilson note 1 also reads him) employ five others: yajamāna, brahman, hotṛ, āgnīdhra, prastotṛ. Anukramaṇī intro gives Agni as deity. Corrected: the two are named as pratiprasthātṛ and adhvaryu rather than loosely as adhvaryu priests; the one hot offering given as his word gharma; the context clause now places the verse after the horses and car of verse 6 instead of a loose list (the hymn has one fount, not fountains). Source line kept.
